notes.1197: Title: Lecture 39 GPS Path Finding; no substantive content.
notes.1198: Objectives roadmap: GPS fundamentals and robotics navigation.
notes.1199: Contents roadmap for GNSS, architecture, coordinates, errors and implementation.
notes.1200: Outdoor delivery, agriculture, surveying and autonomous navigation motivate localization. Global pose anywhere is overbroad: ordinary GNSS position is not full orientation and availability is limited by reception.
notes.1201: Actual GNSS to Localization to Path Planner to Waypoints to Controller to Robot Motion diagram inspected; localization, route choice and feedback control are different functions.
notes.1202: GNSS umbrella and GPS USA, GLONASS Russia, Galileo Europe, BeiDou China, NavIC India, QZSS Japan table inspected. NavIC and QZSS are regional systems; multi-constellation does not imply every system is globally available.
notes.1203: Printed transmission-minus-reception travel-time formula has its sign reversed. Circle equations and three-range planar illustration inspected; noncollinear geometry, consistency and timing assumptions matter.
notes.1204: One range constrains a sphere surface; two ordinary intersecting spheres form a circle. Figures do not imply a solid ball or guaranteed intersection for arbitrary measurements.
notes.1205: Three ideal 3D ranges can leave two candidates. Receiver clock bias gives four unknowns x,y,z,delta-t. Unsquared pseudorange equation is dimensionally meaningful; squared equation followed by pseudorange label is not.
notes.1206: Space, control and user segments plus communication arrows inspected. Ground control estimates orbit/clock and monitors health; users receive broadcasts and solve their own location.
notes.1207: ECEF Earth-centered, Earth-fixed axes: Greenwich equator x, 90E equator y, north pole z. Receiver position computation must not be attributed to satellites.
notes.1208: Latitude, longitude, WGS84 ellipsoidal height and 29.8366N 77.8962E 18m example inspected. Earth-center latitude sketch is geocentric-looking; geodetic latitude uses ellipsoid normal, and ellipsoid height is not mean-sea-level height.
notes.1209: ECEF-to-geodetic and map conversion branch diagram inspected; UTM and local tangent coordinates are illustrative choices, not exclusive 2D versus 3D rules.
notes.1210: Direct, reflected and diffracted path figure inspected. An isolated reflected path is longer; a full receiver's multipath tracking bias need not always have one sign.
notes.1211: Ionospheric and tropospheric code delays plus geometric error amplification inspected. Poor geometry is not itself the same as larger individual ranging error.
notes.1212: Widely spread versus clustered satellite geometry diagrams inspected. Better geometry can reduce amplification without removing all ranging errors.
notes.1213: PDOP is a geometry factor, not a position error in metres. Printed 1–3, 3–6, greater-than-6 categories overlap at 3 and are source heuristics, not universal boundaries.
notes.1214: Road network, destination selection, GNSS localization, map matching, A-star, waypoints and tracking pipeline inspected; pedagogical simulator is not an operational navigation safety claim.
notes.1215: All 12 node coordinate pairs and 19 undirected road edges, including N2–N7 and N6–N11 diagonals, inspected. These are plotting coordinates, not real GPS coordinates.
notes.1216: euclidean uses hypot(dx,dy)/100; adjacency stores round(distance,2) in both directions. Arbitrary scale is not calibrated geography. Unrounded heuristic with rounded edge costs requires admissibility checking.
notes.1217: Actual weighted graph and all edge weights inspected, including 2.69 and 2.66 diagonal shortcuts. Visual crossings are not extra graph nodes unless declared.
notes.1218: Airport N4, Stadium N8, Hospital N9 and Mall N12 destination dictionary inspected. Direct dictionary lookup is not real geocoding.
notes.1219: acquire_gnss_fix samples uniform independent map coordinates, not a satellite measurement or physically justified GNSS noise model. Printed lambda/phi latitude-longitude order conflicts with conventional notation.
notes.1220: Dashboard raw 28.61035 latitude and 77.20186 longitude labels and cyan point inspected; display alone does not prove a WGS84-to-map conversion in shown code.
notes.1221: Nearest Euclidean road-node matching illustration selects N9 Hospital; this differs from nearest road-segment matching.
notes.1222: Projection onto road segments plus heading, trajectory and hidden-state map matching discussed. HMM is one sequence-based method, not mandatory for all navigation systems.
notes.1223: A-star uses graph g+h priority and Euclidean heuristic, not lowest accumulated g alone. Source rounded edges versus unrounded heuristic must be checked before claiming optimality generally.
notes.1224: Highlighted route N9,N10,N11,N12,N8,N4 and reported 9.08 km inspected. Displayed rounded weights total 9.07, so source cost conventions need explicit qualification. Contraction Hierarchies speed statements are not universal timing guarantees. Official notebook execution resolves9.07 versus9.08: search sums rounded edges; waypoints sum raw distances then round cumulative values.
notes.1225: Waypoint dictionary fields index, node ID, optional label and cumulative_km inspected. Displayed cumulative distances 0,1.90,3.91,5.73,7.33,9.08 differ from sum of shown rounded edge costs. Original build_waypoints exactly reproduced all displayed cumulative values from unrounded segment lengths.
notes.1226: Tracking dashboard current waypoint N12 Mall with previous N11 and next N8,N4 inspected. Linked official code should distinguish interpolated animation from closed-loop sensing/control.
notes.1227: Comparison table: snapshot versus fused localization; nearest-node versus segment/sequence matching; undirected distance versus directed restrictions/live cost; A-star versus preprocessed search; fixed route versus rerouting. Examples are not universal production rules.
notes.1228: GNSS uncertainty, outages and fusion with IMU, odometry, LiDAR or SLAM discussed. EKF or factor-graph integration can bridge interruptions but cannot guarantee indefinite bounded drift or safety.
notes.1229: Bibliography only; named books and papers are not claimed read.
